Approved doses: 12 mg (original regimen) and the higher 50 mg loading / 28 mg maintenance regimen. ;; [clinicaltrials] Label section 11 states verbatim: modified antisense oligonucleotide where the 2'-hydroxy groups of the ribofuranosyl rings are replaced with 2'-O-2-methoxyethyl groups and the phosphate linkages are replaced with phosphorothioate linkages; binds a sequence in the intron downstream of exon 7 of the SMN2 transcript. Uniformly 2'-MOE modified, therefore gapmer_design=NA and oligo_class=splice_switching_ASO. Length and PS count not stated in the label, so TBD. Label also documents three strengths (12/28/50 mg per 5 mL), which matches the dose arms extracted from NCT04089566. ;; [clinical_programs] Splice-switching ASO that modifies SMN2 pre-mRNA splicing to increase full-length SMN protein. notes_measurement: [hydrocephalus] grade_provisional. 4-month-old female with Type I SMA. Findings: enlarging head size and lethargy; communicating hydrocephalus; CSF sample showed no evidence of infection. Management: ventriculo-peritoneal shunt placed; nusinersen continued. CONTEXT ROW FOR THE HYDROCEPHALUS INTERPRETATION, included because the ventricle-versus-brain dissociation is the crux of this endpoint: the tominersen arms show GREATER ventricular expansion (m38/m39) but NOT greater whole-brain volume loss than placebo, which argues for CSF-space expansion rather than accelerated atrophy. notes_measurement: [hydrocephalus] grade_provisional. Patient in the tominersen open-label extension (NCT03342053), on monthly intrathecal tominersen. Symptoms (gait difficulty) began after the FIFTH monthly dose and progressed over 3 months. Communicating hydrocephalus; a ventriculo-peritoneal shunt was inserted and mobility returned to the patient's baseline state - grade 3, hydrocephalus requiring intervention, and reversibility recorded as partially_reversible because function recovered only with a permanent shunt. The authors' causality assessment is that this was 'communicating hydrocephalus secondary to a sterile meningitis induced by tominersen', which is a mechanistic hypothesis, not a demonstration. THIS IS A SINGLE CASE REPORT and the paper does not state a denominator; the denominator (1/23 monthly-dosed participants) comes from the trial record, m48. DOSE PROVENANCE: the case report states only 'monthly intrathecal tominersen' without a mg figure; 120 mg is recorded here from the NCT03342053 protocol arm definition ('RO7234292 was administered intrathecally every 28 days'), which the sponsor's CHDI 2021 presentation also links to this case. notes_measurement: [hydrocephalus] grade_provisional. THE MOST IMPORTANT NEGATIVE ROW IN THIS LANE AND ALSO THE WEAKEST - READ THE CAVEAT. This is the largest published survey of neurological findings after intrathecal ASO dosing in non-human primates (28 studies, 1,016 animals). The five sign categories the authors report are: (1) non-adverse transient absence of lower spinal reflexes, dose-related, resolving by 24-48 h; (2) adverse muscle tremor/spasticity during or immediately after injection (one third responded to diazepam, two thirds required euthanasia); (3) ataxia, paresis, nystagmus, urinary incontinence or tremor 30 min to 4 h after dosing; (4) rapidly progressing hind-limb paralysis from spinal cord injury, with MRI-confirmed focal spinal cord necrosis; (5) rare adverse hind-limb paresis or paralysis 2-18 days after dosing. Hydrocephalus, ventriculomegaly and raised intracranial pressure are absent from all five. CAVEAT THAT MUST NOT BE DROPPED: this is a survey of CLINICAL NEUROLOGICAL SIGNS, not of ventricular imaging or morphometry. The paper does not state that ventricular size was measured, and a monkey with mild ventriculomegaly would very likely show no clinical sign at all. readout_value '0_of_1016' therefore means 'no hydrocephalus reported among the clinical signs in 1,016 animals', NOT 'ventricular size was measured in 1,016 animals and found normal'. Treat as weak negative evidence only. notes_measurement: [hydrocephalus] grade_provisional. 21-year-old male, 5q SMA (homozygous SMN1 exon 7-8 deletion, 3 SMN2 copies), symptomatic intracranial hypertension the day after his 12th nusinersen injection. Treated with repeated therapeutic lumbar punctures (40, 30, 25, 20 mL removed) and acetazolamide escalated to 2 x 750 mg daily; opening pressure normalised to 23 cmH2O by day 40. SEVERE CONFOUNDING - the paper's own position: the patient had 'extensive, most likely congenital, bilateral arachnoid cysts with moderate space-occupying effects' AND 'bilateral stenosis of the transverse sinuses', either of which can independently cause intracranial hypertension. The authors conclude only that 'the treatment potentially contributed'. Dose: the paper states 5 mL per injection; 5 mL is the 12 mg approved strength (2.4 mg/mL), so 12 mg is recorded here with that derivation made explicit rather than read directly as a mg figure. Single case report. ;; source_ref_as_cited=J Neuromuscul Dis 2023;10(4), doi 10.3233/JND-230032, PMID 37248913, PMC10357201

notes_measurement: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. PATIENT 1, a girl aged 3 at study initiation with KCNT1 p.R474H epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures. Escalating intrathecal doses of 10, 20, 30 and 40 mg at weeks 0, 2, 4 and 6, then maintenance 40 mg every 8 weeks from week 10, INCREASED TO 60 mg every 8 weeks from week 26. Eight weeks after her 9th intrathecal dose she developed vomiting and apparent discomfort; brain and spine imaging two days later revealed SEVERE COMMUNICATING HYDROCEPHALUS with T2 white-matter change representing transependymal flow but no other parenchymal change. She was at her baseline alertness with normal pupils, normal extraocular movements, no sunset eye sign and normal vital signs. Endoscopic third ventriculostomy with choroid plexus cauterisation showed a CSF OPENING PRESSURE OF 55 cm H2O and produced no improvement over the following two days. After considering a ventriculoperitoneal shunt, the family withdrew from the investigational protocol in favour of palliative care; she died under hospice care three months after the final ASO dose. GRADE 3: hydrocephalus requiring intervention, with a fatal outcome. NOTE: hydrocephalus is primarily another lane's scope; included here because the n-of-1 brief explicitly directs extraction of per-patient hydrocephalus events from this literature. ;; source_ref_as_cited=PMID:41981306; doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04314-9

Consortium-level restatement of the valeriasen experience by the N=1 Collaborative: 'Initially valeriasen was effective at reducing seizure activity in Valeria and a second patient whose treatment commenced after Valeria.
